SECTION 6.12. Financial Covenants .

(a) Interest Coverage Ratio . The Company will not permit the Interest Coverage Ratio, for any period of four consecutive fiscal quarters
of the Company ending on the last day of any fiscal quarter of the Company (commencing with the fiscal quarter ending June 30, 2022), to be less than 3.00 to 1.00.

(b) Total Net Leverage Ratio . The Company will not permit the Total Net Leverage Ratio, on the last day of any fiscal quarter of the
Company ending on or after June 30, 2022, to be greater than (i) 4.00 to 1.00 as of the end of each fiscal quarter of the Company ending on or after June 30, 2022 but prior to March 31, 2024, (ii) 3.75 to 1.00 as of the
end of each fiscal quarter of the Company ending on or after March 31, 2024 but prior to March 31, 2026 and (iii) 3.50 to 1.00 as of the end of each fiscal quarter of the Company ending on or after March 31, 2026; provided
that, upon the written request of the Borrower Representative delivered to the Administrative Agent in connection with any Material Acquisition, the maximum Total Net Leverage Ratio permitted under Section 6.12(b)(i), (ii) or (iii), as
applicable, for each of the four fiscal quarters of the Company ending immediately following the consummation date of such Material Acquisition shall be increased by 0.50 to 1.00 (any such period of four consecutive fiscal quarters being referred to
as a “ Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment ”); provided further, however, that such Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment shall occur (i) only twice during the term of this Agreement, and (ii) only to the extent that no
Event of Default has then occurred and is continuing. Promptly following receipt of notice from the Borrower Representative of its election to give effect to a Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment, the Administrative Agent shall give written notice
of the Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment to the Lenders, and this Agreement shall be automatically amended, without any further action by any party, to reflect such Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment.

ARTICLE VII

Events of Default

SECTION 7.01. Events of Default . Any of the following events shall constitute an “Event of Default”:

(a) the Borrowers shall fail to pay any principal of any Loan or any reimbursement obligation in respect of any LC Disbursement when and as the
same shall become due and payable, whether at the due date thereof or at a date fixed for prepayment thereof or otherwise;

(b) the
Borrowers shall fail to pay any interest on any Loan or any fee or any other amount (other than an amount referred to in Section 7.01(a)) payable under this Agreement or any other Loan Document, when and as the same shall become due and
payable, and such failure shall continue unremedied for a period of three (3) Business Days;

findings.proposedIrEvidence: r3's capacityExpression is kind=EVENT_ACTIVE (a boolean 'is the adjustment window active' flag) with no numeric ratio field; the +0.50 magnitude appears only as free-text in dependsOn.description ('increases... by 0.50 to 1.00') and in the exception.description on r2, never as a structured RATIO value used to actually modify the SCHEDULE thresholds (4.00/3.75/3.50) in r2.
findings.verifierReasoning: The source ties a concrete, operative numeric adjustment (0.50x) to the Material Acquisition election. The proposed IR never encodes this number as a computable value anywhere - only as prose in description fields, which a compliance engine cannot execute. This means the IR, as structured, cannot actually compute the adjusted covenant threshold during an active Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment window, even though both the exception-bearing rule (r2) and the permission rule (r3) are marked sufficiency COMPLETE. This directly confirms the deterministic signal that RATIO 0.5 never appears in the compiled IR, and is a real, operative gap, not a mere citation nuance.

findings.proposedIrEvidence: conditions[1] has conditionType 'UNSUPPORTED' with description 'Such Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment shall occur only twice during the term of the Agreement', yet the parent rule's top-level 'sufficiency' field is 'COMPLETE'.
findings.verifierReasoning: The IR itself internally flags that it could not formally represent the 'only twice during the term of this Agreement' cap - a real, independently operative restriction that limits how many times the 0.50 adjustment can be invoked over the life of the facility. Marking the enclosing rule COMPLETE while one of its own conditions is tagged UNSUPPORTED is an internally inconsistent and overconfident sufficiency claim; a downstream consumer trusting COMPLETE could allow a third or later invocation of the adjustment in violation of the source's twice-only limit.

findings.proposedIrEvidence: conditions[0].referencesDefinitionId is the literal string 'd1', but the only definition object present in the IR's definitions array has definitionId 'ir-definition:673959475f579ccb88b5ed72' (termName 'Material Acquisition'). No definition with id 'd1' exists anywhere in the proposed IR.
findings.verifierReasoning: The condition is plainly intended to depend on the 'Material Acquisition' definition (its own description names 'Material Acquisition'), but the reference id used does not resolve to any actual definition object in the document. This breaks the structural link between the adjustment condition and the (already troubled/PARTIAL) Material Acquisition definition, so a consuming system cannot programmatically confirm what counts as a qualifying acquisition for purposes of triggering the adjustment.

findings.proposedIrEvidence: rules[0].capacityExpression.gatedBy is a bare, time-unbounded COMPARE (ICR GTE 3) with no date/period restriction anywhere in the rule, unlike rules[1] (the Total Net Leverage Ratio rule) which explicitly encodes date boundaries via a SCHEDULE structure.
findings.verifierReasoning: The source expressly scopes the Interest Coverage Ratio test to fiscal quarters commencing with the quarter ending June 30, 2022 - an operative temporal boundary on when the covenant is even tested. The proposed IR for §6.12(a) omits this boundary entirely and is marked sufficiency COMPLETE, creating an inconsistency with how the sibling rule (§6.12(b)) meticulously captures its own date tiers. A reviewer relying on the IR could not tell that the covenant is inapplicable to periods ending before June 30, 2022.

findings.verifierReasoning: Without a resolved link to how these ratios are actually calculated (numerator/denominator components, add-backs, etc.), the covenant's true operative meaning cannot be fully verified from what was provided, and Phase 2 already flagged an unresolved-context issue elsewhere in this same provision. Marking these rules COMPLETE while the metric definitions remain unresolved is a claim I cannot fully validate one way or the other from the evidence given, so I flag it as uncertain rather than a confirmed defect - it may be an expected artifact of how metric definitions are resolved in a later pass, or it may mask a real gap.
